#3498. Witcher 4 Has Fewer People Working On It Than It Did 3 Months Ago, But Just Barely

As part of CD Projekt's latest earnings report, the Polish developer revealed new information about its projects and headcount.

For the quarter that ended on October 31, The Witcher 4 was the company's biggest project by headcount, with 513 people working on it. That's down from 519 people for the quarter that ended on July 31.

For comparison, the number of developers on Cyberpunk 2 rose from 184 to 199 and staffers on the new IP codenamed Hadar jumped from 33 to 34. The codename Sirius game, believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher game, saw its development staff shrink from 84 to 60; the project has undergone numerous shifts throughout its development as CD Projekt reworks the experience.

CD Projekt's total development headcount rose from 1,045 to 1,051.

In terms of money, CD Projekt reported Q3 revenue of 208 million PLN ($51 million USD) and net earnings of 109 million PLN ($26.8 million). CD Projekt spent a lot--more than 177 million PLN ($43.5 million) on development costs during the quarter--but the company's total cash reserves grew by 31 million PLN ($7.6 million USD).

CD Projekt has a number of big projects in the works, including The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past in 2027 and The Witcher 4 in 2028. Cyberpunk 2 is also on the way, but it doesn't have a release window yet. The company is also working on a game with Scopely, the mobile gaming giant owned by Saudi Arabia.

Cyberpunk 2 was in the news recently, as the game's creative director joked that the RPG is now canceled because GTA 6 is so good.

#3497. This Apple Watch Is a Lifehacker 'Gift of the Year' Award Winner, and It's $50 Off Ahead of Black Friday

Apple has three main Apple Watch "lines." There's the flagship, currently the Series 12, which represents Apple's mainstream wearable. For athletes and users who think they'll put their watches through some extreme scenarios, there's the Ultra line, currently the Apple Watch Ultra 4. And while both the Series 12 and Ultra 4 are excellent devices in their own right, they can be pretty pricey (particularly the Ultra). That's why the third category, the SE, is actually best for most people, and Lifehacker's choice for best smartwatch gift of the year. Better yet, the third-generation SE is currently $50 off ahead of Black Friday, perfect for most people asking for an Apple Watch this year.

The SE 3 does just about everything you'd expect an Apple Watch to do. It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple says the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

The majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

If your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, Nov. 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by Dec. 2, 2026.

#3496. WoW: Forever’s Best Buffs Now Work As Intended

World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended.

World Buffs are powerful stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain events. The most common World Buff players see is Warchief's Blessing on the Horde and the new Might of Stormwind for the Alliance, which are granted to all players in Orgrimmar, Stormwind, and their surrounding low-level zones when players on their respective faction turn in a specific high-level quest.

Now that players are reaching endgame and turning in the required quest, these buffs are popping off constantly. They grant a whopping 300 hit points, 15% melee haste, and 10 mana regen per five seconds for one hour. At lower levels, those are some serious stats, particularly the 300 HP.

Unfortunately, players haven't been able to take full advantage of the buffs, as a bug was causing them to be lost when hitting a loading screen. That meant any time a group stepped into a dungeon or took a boat or zeppelin to a new location, their World Buffs would be removed.

That has finally been fixed in the latest update, so players can now enter dungeons with World Buffs to help maximize their damage and health. This should be particularly useful for doing dungeons at a slightly lower level than is intended, as the extra HP and melee haste is definitely noticable.

Blizzard clarified in the patch notes that World Buffs will still be removed when entering raids, so players won't be able to stack as many World Buffs as possible before raid night, as was the case in previous versions of classic WoW. 

Other changes found in the patch notes include a fix for an Uldaman boss that players were exploiting to make fast gold. Another is a fix for "a few spells and abilities" that were causing more weapon-proc effects than intended, likely nerfing the DPS of whatever classes were taking advantage of the bug. You can read the full patch notes below.

Blizzard recently outlined in the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast how it wants to get rid of the idea of "best-in-slot gear," as well as how the game's has overhauled old-school WoW's player-vs.-player systems. In other Forever news, the game's launch has seen more than 15 million characters created so far, with the highest weekly player numbers for WoW in 15 years. 

WoW: Forever November 23 Hotfix Patch Notes

Classes

  • Druid
    • The 4-piece Feralheart set for Druids now correctly grants 4 Energy regeneration every 1 second for 5 seconds.
  • Priest
    • Mind Vision should no longer proc effects.
    • Shadow
      • Fixed an issue where Dark Inspiration was not granting the correct amount of %Spirit increase if Mind Flay was used to activate it.
      • Fixed an issue where Chastise was not usable in Shadowform.
  • Warlock
    • Destruction
      • Fixed an issue where Intensity was not working on Incinerate.
  • Warrior
    • Fixed an issue where players could have and use Mortal Strike from their spellbook, even without the Mortal Strike talent. This does not remove it from their spellbook but prevents it from being used without the talent point spent.

Dungeons

  • Uldaman
    • The Obsidian Sentinel drops loot as intended.

Items

  • The Filcher’s Cowl no longer has a level requirement.

Professions

  • Cooking
    • Boiled Clams, Clam Chowder, Goblin Deviled Clams, Giant Clam Scorcho, Undermine Clam Chowder, and Clam Linguine each now offer the correct Well Fed bonuses and have been recategorized in the recipe list under “Stamina Food”.
    • Murloc Fin Soup has had its recovery and Well-Fed amounts increased to the next tier of food, bringing it closer to other food of that level.
  • Engineering
    • Fixed a bug that caused Goblin Engineer’s Renewal Gift and Gnome Engineer’s Renewal Gift to appear as broken, unusable question marks in the inventory.
    • Fixed a bug that prevented “The Mortar: Reloaded” recipe from being learned upon learning the “Goblin Mortar” recipe.
  • Leatherworking
    • Fixed a bug that prevented Pattern: Centaur Hoofwarmers from being learnable.

Quests

  • Riverglades - Dunston Willis once again runs near the end of the escort “Dunston Checks Out.”
  • Wetlands - After further study, the quest “For Further Study” now has rewards.
  • Wetlands - The quest “Uncovering the Past” now rewards Ironforge reputation.
  • Wetlands - The quest “Gleaning Our Future” now rewards Ironforge reputation.

Races

  • Fixed an issue where Wisp Form could be applied to players while they were alive.

Spells

  • Fixed an issue where a few spells and abilities were causing more weapon procs than intended.
  • Fixed an issue where World Buffs would fall off when changing areas. They will still fall off when entering raid instances.
  • Fixed an issue where Fengus’ Ferocity was granting twice as much Spell Power as intended.
  • Fixed an issue where Darkmoon Faire buffs were granting twice as much power as intended.

I Have A Solution To Dancing With The Stars' Debate Over Dancer Experience

Why DWTS’ Latest Eliminations Should Clue Producers In To What Viewers Want In Future Seasons

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

I can't imagine why anyone would think this.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dancing with the Stars' Season 35 finale just aired on the 2026 TV schedule, and congratulations are in order for Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach. While there's no shortage of fans who are happy for the duo, there are a few disgruntled people who feel his win over Amber Glenn and others came because he lost his prosthetic during his final dance. It's a wild take that's making rounds, and I can't help but roll my eyes at it.

For those who didn't watch DWTS on Tuesday, November 24, on ABC or with a Disney+ subscription, Frech's mishap came during his freestyle dance, which began with him without his prosthetic on. Frech was supposed to slip it on during a quick change segment, and while it was on when he revealed his new look, it quickly fell to the floor. Frech continued to dance until pro dancer Alan Bersten could retrieve the leg, and after a brief pause, Frech reattached it and completed the routine.

The moment received raucous applause from the in-house audience, and the judges awarded him perfect scores. Unfortunately, comments like the one below have since been floating around X, with some arguing Frech received sympathy votes and calling fans ableist for not penalizing him for the incident:

Ezra wanted to be viewed the same as everyone else. Sorry but if that were the case, Amber would’ve won tonight. Ezra won cause his prosthetic fell off during his freestyle so people voted him out of sympathy & cause he was crying/bleeding after. That in itself is ableism.

I can't help but take a deep sigh when reading this take, and admittedly, I'm not the only one who has taken issue this person. With that said, if there are more people out there who quietly believe or think that Ezra's disability is what pushed him across the finish line to be the latest person to win Dancing with the Stars, let me just point out a couple of details.

To chalk Ezra Frech's win up to his final dance of the season discredits a run that was one of the best we've seen this entire season. He was never at the bottom of the leaderboard and was even at the top for a few weeks. Frech never had an off week, not once, which is the type of resilience we expect from Olympic athletes.

Now, looking at the numbers, you'll see Amber Glenn did just as well, and even beat out Ezra for more than a few weeks. As we learned this season, however, DWTS is just as much a popularity contest as it is a dance competition. If Amber should win on scores alone, Jenna Dewan shouldn't have left, and Harry Shum Jr. would've been holding that Mirrorball trophy.

If Ezra Frech gained additional votes in Dancing with the Stars' finale after his freestyle performance, it wasn't out of sympathy. That would imply the dance fell to disaster after he lost his prosthetic, and that simply wasn't the case. Frech not only finished the dance, he completed the routine hardly missing a beat.

Tatyana Ali’s Farewell Message To Jan Ravnik Ahead Of Dancing With The Stars’ Season 35 Finale Has Me In My Feelings

Had Connor Wood, Maura Higgins, Amber Glenn, or Tatyana Ali recovered from a disastrous moment with such poise, I feel confident the judges and audience would've reacted the same way. This is especially true on DWTS' finale night, in which I feel the judges want their scores to impact the end result as little as possible.

If the fans feel Frech's win wasn't justified, then maybe it is time to push for Sharna Burgess' campaign to limit fans to only ten votes. I truly don't think it would've impacted the result at all, but that could've mitigated any perceived advantage Frech had from last-minute voters who might've used their votes otherwise.

In any case, I think summing up Ezra Frech's win to "losing his prosthetic" is offensive and diminishes everything else he did on DWTS. As for Amber, she also would've been a deserving winner, but let's not act like this is the first time this show has had more than one person who could've or should've won.

Dancing with the Stars has one more holiday episode on the way, but the competition is essentially done. I'm excited to tune in and eager to see what other thoughts pop up now that the season is officially over.

#3492. Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”

When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

Dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

The casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He says to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting new additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

In Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy showed me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she says. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” says Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” says Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the big surprises in the ensemble.”

Taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” says Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” says Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”

Pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” says Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

For Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most important for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

When you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a big "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be said for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before new models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

In the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The issue isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

The key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

To avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

If you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

I've been looking forward to seeing Sir Patrick Stewart return as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday, especially knowing he'll be sharing the screen with Sir Ian McKellen again. The two actors have been part of the X-Men franchise for more than 25 years, and I can't imagine the flick without them. Although after Stewart's death in October, his final appearance will carry considerably more emotional weight than anyone originally anticipated. Now Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and directors Joe and Anthony Russo are opening up about Stewart's last day on set for the upcoming Marvel movie, and I'm already getting emotional.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly, Feige recalled a moment when the legendary actor addressed the crew after completing his work. Nobody knew for certain what it would mean at the time, but looking back, it sounds like Stewart knew he was saying goodbye. Marvel's head honcho revealed:

He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew. We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.

Well, that got me. Stewart died at 86 on Oct. 29, making Doomsday his final on-screen performance. Knowing he apparently recognized the significance of that moment makes the story particularly heartbreaking.

I've always admired Stewart's ability to bring such extraordinary warmth and humanity to Charles Xavier. Even when the X-Men movies weren't particularly great, his presence could make a scene work. There's something incredibly moving about imagining the actor who spent decades portraying a mentor taking a moment to address the people who helped bring his final performance to life. Anthony Russo admitted that Stewart's farewell carried a weight that everyone seemed to recognize, even if nobody wanted to acknowledge what it might mean:

I think it was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again.

The director also revealed that Stewart was dealing with significant health challenges while filming. According to Russo, the actor's determination to deliver the performance was evident to everyone around him. And it wasn't easy watching someone they admired push himself so hard. He continued:

It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew. You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.

I have a feeling that sentiment will carry over to audiences when the film finally arrives. Stewart first portrayed Xavier in the 2000s X-Men, eventually becoming one of the franchise's most recognizable faces. He returned for several sequels, delivered a particularly devastating performance in 2017's Logan, and later surprised MCU fans with an appearance in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

Now, more than a quarter-century after his first appearance, he'll be returning alongside McKellen's Magneto. Joe Russo revealed that the longtime friends share an emotional scene about forgiveness, which could be especially difficult to watch under the circumstances.

Another detail from the interview makes this farewell even sadder. Stewart was reportedly offered a role in Avengers: Secret Wars as well, but chose to appear only in Doomsday. Feige also confirmed that Marvel is working on a tribute to the actor for the upcoming release.

I can't help thinking about how many people grew up with Stewart's Professor X, myself included. His portrayal helped define what new superhero movies could accomplish emotionally long before cinematic universes became the norm.

Knowing his final day involved such a heartfelt farewell to the people around him makes me appreciate his commitment even more. Whatever happens to Charles Xavier in Doomsday, I'm grateful Stewart got one last opportunity to play him.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters December 18 as part of the 2026 movie release schedule. I'll be bringing tissues.

#3488. How to Cancel Your Amazon Prime Membership After Black Friday and Cyber Monday

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

One of Amazon’s biggest sales of the year, Black Friday and Cyber Monday, is set to start Nov. 27, but many early deals are already rolling in. To take advantage of everything the sale has to offer, you’re going to need to be a Prime Member. If you sign up for an Amazon Prime account to take advantage of the sale but decide you don’t want to pay for an ongoing membership, you’ll need to cancel your subscription before the end of your free trial.

You can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

As mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

Finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

Circana has released its latest monthly sales report for the US video game industry, and in terms of game sales, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 led the way.

#3486. Decoding Kate Middleton’s “Tourdrobe” for Her Trip to India

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a new confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

The dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

Wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

“It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley says. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”

#3485. Tovah Feldshuh Reveals If She'll Return to 'Nobody Wants This' After Drama

Tovah Feldshuh revealed whether she will appear on Nobody Wants This season 4 after offscreen tension over Adam Brody‘s public support for Palestine.

“Do I hope for [my character] Bina to be written in? Heavily so,” Feldshuh, 77, exclusively told Us ahead of PaleyImpact’s “One-on-One with Tovah Feldshuh” panel at the Paley Museum in New York City on Monday, November 23.

Feldshuh weighed in on whether the hit Netflix series would have larger conversations about the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine, adding, “I imagine there’ll be no politics whatsoever about Zionism. But nonetheless, Bina is the sturdy anchor to old world [Jewish] values — some of which are cliche because they work and they’ve worked for centuries.”

The actress ensured she’s fully prepared to continue playing Brody’s onscreen mother.

“I hope Bina lives for at least five seasons,” she continued. “And I love working on Nobody Wants This and with everybody in the cast.”

Nobody Wants This, which premiered in 2024, follows the love story between agnostic Joanne (Kristen Bell) and unconventional rabbi Noah (Brody). While Nobody Wants This has resonated with viewers throughout the years, the show recently made headlines when Brody, 46, shared his personal political views.

“I have spoken a lot about [the Israel and Palestine conflict] privately. I haven’t spoken much about it publicly,” he told GQ in October. “Put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine.”

Erin Foster, who cocreated the show, later spoke out on the “complicated” situation regarding her and Brody’s different perspectives.

“I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing,” she said on the “Not Skinny But Not Fat” podcast as Brody’s comments went viral. “While I love Adam, I also disagree with him. And that’s OK.”

Feldshuh also disagreed with Brody’s point of view, sharing more insight into their dynamic while speaking with Us on Monday.

“After he said his comments, he asked to see me. So we’ve talked privately about it,” she said before clarifying there was “no animosity” between her and Brody. “But [there is] profound disagreement. We’ll see hopefully if he will — based on fact and history — change his point of view.”

Feldshuh stood by her past statements of support for Israel.

“I’ve never directly addressed Adam in public, nor will I. We are colleagues so we can disagree without being disagreeable,” she explained. “However, I’m sure everybody is very clear about how I stand and this isn’t a political statement. This is a statement based on whether or not I have a right to live.”

Feldshuh concluded: “I’m not Israeli and neither is Erin Foster. But fortunately for me, she agrees with me and that’s lucky. I will not cross swords with Adam. He plays my son, and you know what else? He’s been an incredible friend to me. When they showed my documentary at the temple that hosted us, who came out of all the cast? Adam Brody. He sat next to me.”

Looking ahead, Feldshuh shared what she would like to explore on Nobody Wants This.

“I would love a flashback,” she said, also suggesting a possible cameo from her former Crazy Ex-Girlfriend costars. “Rachel [Bloom], of course needs to come on. Also Santino Fontana — I thought he was great. I thought Donna Lynne Champlin was fabulous.”

Nobody Wants This is streaming on Netflix.

#3484. The Witcher 4 Wants To Be The GTA 6 Of The Witcher Franchise

There's been a massive gap between new entries in The Witcher series, and for The Witcher 4, developer CD Projekt Red aims to make it the GTA 6 of the series, with a noticeable leap in quality. In its Q3 earnings call, the studio says it has been inspired by the technological and gameplay advancements Rockstar Games has made with GTA 6--especially when compared to 2013's GTA 5--and hopes players will feel the same way when they jump into The Witcher 4.

"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski (via Eurogamer). "But I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4--I think so, yes. It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

When The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt was first released in 2015, it was hailed for raising the bar for open-world adventure games. Its side-quests were singled out for being narratively dense, full of micro-consequences, and on par with the main campaign missions. In the years since, numerous open-world games have used The Witcher 3 as a blueprint, with notable examples being the Assassin's Creed trilogy of Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla alongside Sony's Horizon Zero Dawn and Ghost of Tsushima.

Eleven years later, that bar has been raised again with GTA 6, which offers emergent, player-driven open-world chaos through multiple systems. The world of The Witcher is naturally very different from the consumerism-focused setting of GTA 6, but if The Witcher 4 builds on its predecessor's strengths and adds more nuance to those gameplay mechanics, we could be in for something special.

CDPR also said it's trying to make The Witcher 4 more appealing to mainstream audiences, but it hasn't detailed exactly how it plans to do that. "Our games are different, and they require a certain different approach--we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: This is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future," Nowakowski said.

Currently, over 500 people are working on The Witcher 4, and CDPR has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the game ahead of its targeted 2028 release. The studio is also chipping away at Cyberpunk 2, but after the launch of GTA 6, the game's creative director joked about canceling it, saying Rockstar's game set a high standard for open-world games.

Taylor Swift has been dealing with a lot this week. Of course, there’s the expose about her that led to comments about Ugg boots and more going viral. Now, a lawsuit she’s involved in has come back into the spotlight, as she’s asking a judge to intervene in it.

Earlier this year, Maren Flagg, who performs under the name Maren Wade, filed a trademark lawsuit against Taylor Swift. She claimed she trademarked “Confessions of a Showgirl” in 2015, and she was of the opinion that Swift’s album, The Life of a Showgirl, impacted her brand. She also said (via Variety) that the album and her brand “share the same structure, the same dominant phrase, and the same overall commercial impression.” She asked for an injunction to stop Swift from using The Life of a Showgirl brand.

In response, Swift’s lawyers called this argument “absurd.” Now, according to a new report from TMZ, the singer is asking a judge to intervene in all of this. New documents showed that the pop star did not approve of Flagg’s latest efforts to have their legal battle in California, as her motion read:

Wade is arguing that she can sue the singer in California because she performs there. Swift did perform at the Academy Museum Gala in LA recently. However, according to the pop star’s team, a performance in the state does not mean she can be sued there, and she doesn’t have a legal connection to California.

Now, as this is all unfolding, Taylor Swift is also at the center of many other stories. Most controversially, the Vanity Fair expose about her is making waves. It did not paint Swift in a good light; however, it’s also being met with a lot of backlash.

There’s also the whole issue with the shrubs and security Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are working to implement around their home in Ohio. Those were ultimately approved; however, many people who live in that neighborhood were not happy about it.

However, there are good things going on too. Just last week, Swift performed at the CMA Awards, and she’s been on the Oscar campaign trail for her Toy Story 5 song. She released encore songs for The Life of a Showgirl this fall, too, and as always, the theorizing about when we might see Taylor Swift (Taylor’s Version) and/or her 13th album is ongoing.

Oh, and she’s been spotted in the stands cheering on her husband, Travis Kelce, at his games. Speaking of Kelce and Swift, they had the wedding of the year this summer at Madison Square Garden. And those who went seemingly have nothing but the best things to say about the “intimate” event.

All this is to say, Taylor Swift has been taking the good with the bad, and that’s been happening throughout her career. Now, as we learn more about this lawsuit that seems to have a new wrinkle, we’ll keep you posted.

#3481. GTA 6 Modders Are Trying To Vibe-Code A PC Port, And It’s Not Going Well

PC modders are racing to get GTA 6 playable on PC after the leak of the game's complete Xbox build, but so far it doesn't look too promising.

GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games haven't been sitting idle either, as one of the leads behind the Project Leonida Discord group claimed in now-deleted social media posts that they were stepping away from the mammoth task of getting GTA 6 to run on PC. Project Leonida has also been taken down, but it's not the only group trying to get GTA 6 running outside of PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

None of these groups have succeeded yet, and as Twitter user Chasm detailed online, maybe relying heavily on AI tools isn't the way to go. Dev streams have been full of users leveraging generative AI tools to do something, with several prompts being absolute gems of wishful thinking. Here's a snippet of what people have been throwing at Google's Antigravity, while butchering the English language:

  • Continue working and do apply ever part of the code
  • make no mistakes
  • You need todo one thing at a time not a little bit of everything
  • we need all the game start like the rockstar launch so on that stuff, not in game stuff yet
  • work faster
  • there has to be a faster way to iterate than this

Even with an army of enthusiasts throwing prompts and cash at generative AI, a copied version of GTA 6 still seems far out of reach. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick commented in March that the idea of using AI and simply pushing a button to make a hit game was "laughable," and he referenced the music industry, which is grappling with a flood of AI slop to top streaming platforms. "Right now [in music] there are programs that allow you to put out a prompt and get a professionally recorded song spit back out at you. It sounds like a song, but I defy you to listen to it more than once. It's great to send as a greeting card to your partner on their birthday, but that's about it," Zelnick said.

Whatever progress is made in the GTA 6 PC port scene, don't expect it to last long before Take-Two's lawyers pounce. The publisher hasn't shied away from protecting its IP in the past, and takedown notices for any future GTA 6-related projects seem likely. In related GTA 6 news, you can read up on how the game has given Pornhub a hard time and how it became the biggest launch in PlayStation history.

#3479. GTA 6’s Fake Tunnel Is A Great Way To Turn Your Muscle Car Into Scrap Metal

GTA 6 has no shortage of forces trying to put a damper on your crime spree, but the long arm of the law might be the least of your worries if you're planning a successful caper in Vice City. As players have discovered, the greatest threat to a clean getaway might just be an impressive mural, as they've smashed their vehicles right into an unforgiving wall that looks like it was ripped straight out of a Road Runner cartoon.

Located in Vice City's Decor District, this piece of street art resembles a tunnel going under the nearby overpass, and at high speed, it's pretty convincing--something I discovered to my dismay, totaling my pretty sweet muscle car in the process. Does anyone have an industrial-strength magnet so that I can start working out these dents?

It's a delicious bit of trolling from Rockstar Games: the kind of design choice that would make Looney Tunes legend Tex Avery proud with how effective it is. Numerous players have been caught out, and this is just one of many little secrets and Easter eggs hidden in the game. Fortunately, a gas station was nearby, and my muscle car limped to it for a quick repair.

As GTA 6 prepares to celebrate its first record-breaking week of release, players have made plenty of discoveries. The Bigfoot mystery has been solved, you can hop into a portal to visit Vice City during the '80s, and there's even an island where bored rich people will hunt you. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#3477. Witcher 4 Won’t Be A PS5 Exclusive After New Deal With PlayStation

CD Projekt Red and Sony Interactive Entertainment just announced a marketing deal for The Witcher 4, but that doesn't mean the game will be exclusive to PlayStation.

CD Projekt Red's Michał Nowakowski said on social media, "Just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform."

The marketing deal could be similar to the one between Rockstar and Sony for GTA 6, where GTA 6 was given preferential treatment on PS5 in a number of ways in the marketing campaign.

Beyond The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red is making Cyberpunk 2, a new IP codenamed Hadar, a new game believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher title, and a remake of the original Witcher. On the mobile side, CD Projekt Red is working with Scopely on a new game that hasn't been announced yet.

The Witcher 4 now has more than 500 people working on it, and the game is expected to release in 2028. Given that timing, The Witcher 4 likely won't be on a disc because Sony won't support game discs beginning in January 2028.

That being said, CD Projekt Red is promising that The Witcher 4 will have some kind of physical goodies for fans.

In other news about The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red recently discussed the game in comparison to GTA 6.

"Of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4–I think so, yes," Nowakowski said. "It’s been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.”

#3476. The Best Headphones of 2026 Are Over $110 Off for Black Friday

One of the best headphone deals right now is for my favorite headphones: Sony's 1000X series has been around since 2016, with each new model improving on the previous iteration; the latest being the Sony WH-1000XM6, released in 2025. These are the best over-ear headphones I tested in 2025 (or ever, really). Right now, you can get the WH-1000XM6 headphones for $348 (originally $459.99), their lowest price ever during the early Black Friday sale from Amazon.

The XM6 headphones improve on what were already excellent headphones. Sony upped the count of microphones from eight to 12 when compared to the XM5, which improves more than just how well you sound to someone on a phone call. The microphones are used in almost all of its features, like ANC, Adaptive Sound Control, and the headphones' Ambient Sound mode. They hear your surroundings to adapt their features accordingly. If you switch from a noisy room to a quiet one, the XM6 can switch from ANC to "aware mode" (if you have Adaptive Sound Control on).

These headphones have a lot more features that you can nerd out on in their companion app. The audio quality is second to none, with the fully customizable EQ giving you plenty of options to get the sound how you like it. I really like being able to see what codec you're listening to in the app's main menu. That way, there's no guessing if you're getting the best audio quality or not. They will give you 30 hours of battery life with ANC on and 40 hours of juice with ANC off. There's an AUX (3.5mm) jack for wired listening, which is a nice touch for audiophiles who still rock iPod Classics (or is that just me?).

The XM6s were not just the best headphones of 2025, but are still the best ones of 2026 and likely to be the best ones for years to come. For $348, you'll be securing the best for a record-low price.

#3475. 'DWTS' Champ Ezra Frech Says He 'Blacked Out' During Historic Freestyle

Ezra Frech made history as the first amputee and youngest man to win Dancing With the Stars alongside partner Daniella Karagach — but the victory still hasn’t set in.

“Last night was crazy. … I can’t believe this happened,” Frech, 21, said on Good Morning America just hours after the season 35 finale aired on Tuesday, November 24. “I can’t believe we got that opportunity to represent [the disabled community].”

For the season finale, the remaining five couples performed three separate dances, including the fan-favorite freestyle. Frech and Karagach, 33, earned a combined score of 90 out of 90 from judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Bruno Tonioli and Derek Hough, landing them in a three-way tie with Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov and Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas.

Before being announced as the winners, Frech and Karagach experienced a mishap in their live freestyle when the Paralympian struggled to get his prosthetic blade onto his leg.

“We started our freestyle without the prosthetic, that was a creative choice, and then things went a little off script,” Frech said on GMA. “I wasn’t able to suction my leg on and I knew it wasn’t on. Sometimes when that happens, it’ll re-suction, but it didn’t. It came off. She told me to put it on mid-dance, I kinda blacked out.”

He continued, “When it came off, I was like, ‘I’m doing the rest of the dance without my leg on.’ And I heard [Daniella] go, ‘Put your leg on!'”

Karagach added, “I saw his face, I was like, ‘If I don’t tell him to put his leg on, he’s gonna do the whole dance without it.'”

When asked how he planned on celebrating his historic win, Frech said, “The first thing I’m gonna do is just go home and be with my family, probably, and get some nice relaxation time. I mean, everybody on the cast knows, it’s a crazy ride and there’s so much that goes into it.”

He added, “But honestly, the celebration was getting to spend the night on the private jet coming here with all you guys. I love this cast so much, I have so much respect and admiration for each and every single one of you. We’ve become so close … and so we had a lot of fun on the plane tonight.”

Prior to the finale, some of the finalists admitted they experienced nerves leading up to the finale and questioned whether they would make it to the last episode.

“I was waiting for them to finish the sentence,” Connor Wood said in an exclusive interview with Us after the November 17 semifinals while reflecting on hearing his and Rylee Arnold‘s names called first. “I go, ‘What do we do? You want us to dance again? You want us to do our dance again, you sick freaks?'”

Following the finale, Wood, 31, gushed over the connection he formed with Frech throughout the competition. “If I was a betting man — and God, I wish I had — I would’ve made a lot of money tonight. … He’s been my little brother since day one, did not need an introduction. We immediately just, like, connected,” he told Extra. “A lot like Rylee and I, honestly.”

Wood continued, “I see him, I see his perseverance, the way he carries himself. He talks me through stuff. … Just seeing him tonight, that’s a winner.”

Dancing With the Stars airs on ABC and Disney+ Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET.

WWE moved away from Survivor Series’ traditional format of all multi-man matches in the mid 90s. I get where Vince McMahon and company were coming from. It’s harder to build when you have so many moving parts, and it was harder to get people to buy PPVs back in the day without world title matches. In an effort to get back to the spirit of Survivor Series, Triple H has used a men’s and women’s WarGames match the last few years to keep that 5 on 5 format, but the event doesn't have quite the same prestige it once did. This year, however, he also threw in an old school Survivor Series elimination match, and the build has been the best thing on WWE television in months.

Seriously, if you have not been watching the segments for the United States versus Mexico match over the past several weeks, you have missed out big time. Cody Rhodes was picked as captain of the United States team. He quickly added CM Punk, who promptly appointed himself as co-captain. Since then, they’ve been trying to fill out the roster, and it’s led to a nice showcase for team members LA Knight and Je’Von Evans, as well as a fun segment with proposed team member The Miz and maybe the best segment of the entire year with a 70-something year old Hacksaw Jim Duggan who joined the team and then promptly quit after seeing a highlight reel of their Mexican opponents. I cannot freaking wait for the match, especially after Seth Rollins was added to maximize the drama.

Fortunately, there are some other exciting matches to look forward to, as well. The men’s War Games will feature the Bloodline against the 946, the latter of whom feel like they’re building some real momentum and are an actual threat to win. The women’s War Games match hasn’t had quite the same build, but it still features some top talent and should be a good showcase for younger talent as well. Throw in a pretty compelling Women’s World Championship match with Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch, and the card is really pretty solid.

Before I get into what I think is going to happen in each match, you can check out how I’ve done on predictions. I’ve given my take ahead of every PLE since WrestleMania 38, and while I’m not going to main event WrestleMania with this win-loss record, I could be competing for a midcard championship. Here’s a quick snapshot of the bigger WWE PLEs this year, as well as the overall record…

With all due respect to Team Mexico and especially Penta who currently holds the Money In The Bank Briefcase, this match is lopsided on paper. Cody, CM Punk and Seth are three of the biggest stars in the entire company, and Rhdoes especially does not lose unless it’s in a very key spot or in service of building to something larger or very memorably at WrestleMania 39, both. This match, however, feels like it’s really building toward something larger. It feels like a Mega Powers explode situation.

There’s been so much talk about Cody Rhodes possibly turning heel after punting Randy Orton, but I think it’s more likely we’re going to see CM Punk turn on Cody, or potentially turn full heel, as he’s clearly irate about Rhodes adding his longtime enemy Seth Rollins to the team. At minimum, the story of this match is going to be about the simmering tension between Rhodes, Punk and Rollins. Now, does that mean they’re going to actually lose the match? Not necessarily.

They could fight amongst themselves and wind up with some shock eliminations, or they could fight through the tension and win, pushing the inevitable turn further down the road.

I feel like the long-term goal here is to move us into a feud with Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez. Rumors have swirled that Perez was originally slated to win Money In The Bank. She appeared in Morgan’s backstage segment with her this past Monday. Lynch has talked about how Judgment Day is holding her back. She’s clearly going to play a factor here in some way. It would be easy to say she’ll turn on Morgan and cost her the belt, but I don’t think that’s going to happen.

First, I don’t think there’s been enough teasing of a Judgment Day break-up. Fans have speculated about it forever, but we haven’t gotten nearly enough friction since Finn left to maximize the possible payoff here. Doing it now would be underbaked and stupid. Second, I think what Roxanne actually wants is a shot at the title, and she’s going to ruin that if Morgan loses the title. So, I think she’s going to help her ensure Liv keeps it.

Throw in the fact that Liv is already committed to the John Cena classic, and I feel pretty confident she’s going to hold onto the belt here.

For the longest time, I was sure we were headed toward an Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair break-up, but curiously, WWE really hasn’t teased much friction between the two lately, not since Tatum Paxley's early main roster promotion. Without that dynamic, this really just feels like a run of the mill babyfaces vs heels match that we would get at a house show.

Maybe there’s an angle I’m not seeing here or one that will emerge during the show, but absent that, I’m going to pick the babyfaces because when in doubt, always pick the babyfaces. That’s just a standard wrestling rule, and given I think there’s a potential for a lot of heels to win on this card, it makes even more sense to go with the babyfaces.

Predicted Winner: Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley.

This is the moment where we find out how WWE really feels about 946 and Royce Keys. They’ve been the primary antagonists on the show for months and have been presented like really dangerous and unhinged monsters we should take seriously. If they lose here, it kind of feels like that’s the end. I mean I’m not saying they’re going to get released, but it feels like that’s the end of the audience taking them seriously. They’re the ones stepping up and trying to prove they’re main event players. If they lose in their first big PLE match trying to do that, then that tells the audience all they need to know.

I think WWE believes in them more than that. I think they also believe in the recently added Cruz Montana, and I think they see the 946 as another chance to push Carmelo. They really need this win in a way the Bloodline doesn’t, and if they do win, it would make all the sense in the world to build toward Keys getting a legit title shot at Royal Rumble against Roman Reigns. He would be a big underdog in that match, but he would at least be coming off some momentum from a victory here.

I think the 946 really needs to win, but WWE also almost never has the Bloodline actually lose. So, do I feel confident about this? No.

#3471. Prince William Reportedly Wants to Strip Prince Harry of His Titles

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”

Originally published in Vanity Fair France.

#3470. Is GTA 6 Too Easy? Rockstar Weighs In

Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and one of the things people are talking about is the game's difficulty level. Some are saying it's too easy. Rockstar boss Rob Nelson has now entered the conversation, telling Destructoid that Rockstar's data showed that GTA 4 was "a little too punishing in places" and GTA 5 was "perhaps too easy." So with GTA 6, the team trying to "land somewhere in the middle."

GTA 6 has no defined difficulty levels, which is in keeping with the franchise's tradition. That said, players can adjust things like aiming controls, while players can unlock cheat codes to make the game easier or harder.

Design producer Scott Mitchell, meanwhile, said the fail states in GTA 6 were designed to feel "appropriate."

“We wanted to keep things open and not limit the players’ use of mechanics, such as stealth, but we did also want to make sure we retained the cinematic, high production value, explosive sequences that we’re known for, and people expect. It feels like we’ve managed to strike a good balance," he explained.

Also in the interview, Nelson said figuring out the difficulty level for GTA 6 is itself challenging because the designers themselves know enemy positions better than anyone after playing and testing the game so much.

"There’s a real process in unpicking some of that to create an experience most players will be able to enjoy, rather than endure," Nelson said. "The game is so big, and has such a wide range of content that we can really lean into that, making certain open-world content--compounds and fronts for example---more difficult, to give players seeking a challenge something to sink their teeth into as well.”

GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one.

For more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of five things to do first.

#3469. Jennifer Lopez Makes Rare Comment About 'Tough' Marc Anthony Divorce

Jennifer Lopez makes a rare comment about her 2011 split from ex-husband Marc Anthony in her upcoming concert special.

“After my third divorce — that’s when I really started getting good at it,” the “Let’s Get Loud” singer, 57, tells her Las Vegas audience with a laugh in The JLO Show, which premieres on CBS and Paramount+ Thursday, November 26. “It’s not funny. It’s funny! It is funny. It’s not funny.”

Lopez candidly admits on stage that her separation from Anthony, 58, was “a really tough time,” as the couple had welcomed their twins, Max and Emme, only three years prior.

“It was one of those moments in life where you’re just about to give up on it all,” she reflects. “You’re just like, ‘I’ve given up on love. I’m giving up on life, the whole thing.’ But I had these two little baby twins, you know?”

The Grammy nominee tells the crowd that she decided to call one of her “mentors,” motivational speaker and self-help author Louise Hay, for some guidance at the time.

“I said, ‘I don’t know what I’m going to do. I don’t know how to go on,'” she recalls. “And she said, ‘Jennifer, you’re a dancer, right?’ I said, ‘Yes, I am.’ And she said, ‘When you’re learning a dance and you get the steps wrong, what do you do?’ I said, ‘I just keep going until I get the steps right.’ And she said, ‘That’s it, Jennifer. Always keep dancing.'”

Lopez and Anthony wed in 2004 and finalized their divorce in 2014. She was previously married to Ojani Noa from 1997 to 1998 and Cris Judd from 2001 to 2003.

The Hustlers actress went on to say “I do” a fourth time, eloping with Ben Affleck in 2022. The pair, who first dated in the early aughts, called it quits again in 2024 and divorced in 2025.

These days, Lopez is not thinking about dating again.

“I’ve learned a lot over the past 20 years, but also the past couple of years have really been about becoming more self-aware and really understanding what love is,” she recently told Variety. “I had a real idea about love as a little girl, and moving through this crazy life that I found myself in, I realized that what I thought love was really isn’t love.”

The “Jenny From the Block” singer continued, “Love is a secure, safe feeling. Marriages, people can promise you the world and commit and do all the ceremonious things and do all these big gestures, but love is a different thing than that. It’s a very different thing than that. So, the weddings and the marriages, I realize they’re not the thing, and even the promises are not the thing. It’s the actions, it’s the showing up, it’s the understanding. It’s not the leaving. It’s the being consistent.”

The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas airs on CBS Thursday, November 26, at 8 p.m. ET. An extended version will be available to stream on Paramount+.

In line with the company’s design language, these headphones feature transparent elements and bold, geometric detailing that make them stand out from typical matte-black pairs. But the appeal goes beyond the look. These IP52-rated headphones use 40mm drivers, hybrid ANC, and both USB-C and 3.5mm connectivity. They also support high-res audio via LDAC, while Nothing’s companion app gives you basic and advanced EQ controls for adjusting the sound. Battery life is impressive, too, stretching to 35 hours with ANC on and up to 80 hours with it switched off.

But the hardware alone doesn’t define the experience—Nothing’s control scheme is what makes these wireless headphones stand out. Instead of touch panels or clunky buttons, you get a satisfying volume scroll wheel (they call it the Roller), a multi-function Paddle for track navigation, and a customizable button that can switch EQ profiles or noise modes. You also get spatial audio and multipoint Bluetooth support, which work well across Android and iOS.

That said, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. Performance-wise, the ANC handles low-end noise well (think airplane engines and AC hum) but struggles with sharper, unexpected sounds like clanging dishes or chatter nearby. As for its sound profile, it leans towards the punchier side, especially with a bit of EQ tweaking in the app, but you’ll need to put in some effort if you want the best results, notes this PCMag review.
